# Column Mapping Report — fischertechnik_lab_B (significant-hilarious-cuscus)

## 1. Dataset Summary

- **Source**: `work_files/eventlog.parquet` → cleaned: `work_files/eventlog_cleaned.parquet`
- **Shape**: 1,383 rows × 20 columns (raw); 1,383 rows × 12 columns (cleaned)
- **Structure**: lifecycle layout — exactly 3 rows per activity instance (`scheduled` → `start` → `complete`), 461 instances, 38 cases (workpieces), 20 activities, 15 resources, 9 process-model variants.
- **Time span**: t0 = 2021-06-30T15:24:34Z, horizon T ≈ 5,943.7 s (~99 min).
- **Outcomes**: 452 success, 9 failure (kept — real factory behavior; HTTP 418/401 on the `complete` row).
- **No duplicate rows**; no missing values in key columns.

## 2. Column Mapping

| Column | Meaning | Simulation Role | Sim-Relevant | Action |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `time:timestamp` | Timestamp of the lifecycle transition (ISO8601, mixed precision) | Request time on `scheduled` row; **service start** on `start` row | Yes | Keep; parse to seconds. Actual duration = `operation_end_time` − `time:timestamp` on `start` rows only |
| `operation_end_time` | Operation end timestamp (ISO8601) | **Service end** (preferred over `time:timestamp` of the `complete` row) | Yes | Keep; parse to seconds |
| `lifecycle:transition` | Transition type: `scheduled` / `start` / `complete` | Lifecycle column | Yes | Keep |
| `lifecycle:state` | `assigned` (scheduled) / `inProgress` (start) / `success` / `failure` (complete) | Outcome column; 9 failures retained | Yes | Keep |
| `event_id` | Integer id shared by the 3 rows of an instance (1002–1483) | Redundant instance key | No | **Drop** (keep `identifier:id`) |
| `identifier:id` | Activity-instance id (e.g. `a_15513`), unique per instance | Instance column linking the 3 lifecycle rows | Yes | Keep |
| `process_model_id` | Process-model / product variant (WF_101…WF_1107), 9 values | Variant column | Yes | Keep |
| `case` | Workpiece id, e.g. `WF_101_13` (prefix = process model, 100% consistent) | Case column | Yes | Keep |
| `concept:name` | Activity name (e.g. `/ov/burn`, `/vgr/pick_up_and_transport`), 20 values | Activity column | Yes | Keep |
| `requested_service_url` | REST URL of the service call; resource query param matches `org:resource` 100% | Redundant (resource already mapped); carries size/thickness for burn | No | **Drop** (parameters carry the same info) |
| `org:resource` | Executing resource (vgr_1/2, hbw_1/2, mm_1/2, ov_1, hw_1, wt_1/2, sm_1, …), 15 values | Resource column | Yes | Keep |
| `planned_operation_time` | Planned duration, timedelta string (e.g. `0 days 00:00:47`) | Planned processing time | Yes | Keep; **parse to seconds** (22 distinct values, 5–222 s) |
| `parameters` | Dict string of activity parameters (positions, hbw slot, burn size/thickness, NFC flag); 1 missing on a `complete` row | Activity parameters (routing/variant detail) | Yes | Keep |
| `case:concept:name` | Identical to `case` (100%) | Redundant | No | **Drop** |
| `SubProcessID` | UUID present only on `start` rows (459/461) | Redundant instance detail | No | **Drop** |
| `current_task` | Free-text task description, only on `start` rows | Redundant narrative | No | **Drop** |
| `response_status_code` | HTTP code on `complete` rows (200 / 418×7 / 401×2) | Redundant with `lifecycle:state` (success↔200, failure↔418/401, 100% consistent) | No | **Drop** |
| `complete_service_time` | Full response time scheduled→complete incl. queueing (timedelta string), only on `complete` rows | Reference metric (mean 73.6 s vs 30.4 s actual service) | Yes | Keep (do not use as service duration) |
| `human_workstation_green_button_pressed` | 1/0 flag, only on `/hw/human_review` instances (87 rows) | Human-intervention detail; not needed for core simulation | No | **Drop** |
| `unsatisfied_condition_description` | Precondition-failure detail (NFC/light-barrier/warehouse errors), only on the 9 failed instances | Diagnostic detail of failures | No | **Drop** |

## 3. Log Schema (confirmed via `set_log_schema`)

- **Layout**: lifecycle — one row per transition; 3 rows per instance.
- **case_col**: `case` | **activity_col**: `concept:name` | **resource_col**: `org:resource` | **variant_col**: `process_model_id`
- **start_col**: `time:timestamp` | **end_col**: `operation_end_time` (preferred over `complete`-row timestamp)
- **lifecycle_col**: `lifecycle:transition` | **instance_col**: `identifier:id`
- **enabled_value**: `scheduled` (queue entry / request) | **start_value**: `start` | **complete_value**: `complete`
- **state_col**: `lifecycle:state` | success: `success` | failure: `failure`
- **Validation**: 461 instances, 38 cases, 20 activities, 15 resources; `enabled_observed_frac = 1.0` (waiting times fully observable); `end_missing = 0`; no warnings. Sample verified: e.g. `/hbw/unload` on `hbw_2`: enabled 0.0 s → start 3.56 s → end 55.91 s (≈ start + 52 s planned).
- **Duration convention**: actual service duration = `operation_end_time − time:timestamp` on `start` rows only (mean 30.4 s, min 0.0, max 218.7 s, no negatives). `complete_service_time` records the full response time (scheduled → complete, incl. queueing; mean 73.6 s, max 1,079 s) and is kept only as a reference metric.

## 4. Excluded Columns

`event_id`, `case:concept:name`, `SubProcessID`, `current_task`, `response_status_code`, `requested_service_url`, `unsatisfied_condition_description`, `human_workstation_green_button_pressed` (8 columns; all redundant or diagnostic-only).

## 5. Cleaning Summary

- Dropped 8 columns (above).
- Drop rows with missing values in key columns (`identifier:id`, `case`, `concept:name`, `org:resource`, `time:timestamp`, `operation_end_time`, `lifecycle:transition`, `lifecycle:state`): **0 rows removed** (no missing values in these columns).
- Duplicate rows: none.
- Result: 1,383 rows × 12 columns → `eventlog_cleaned.parquet`.
- All 9 `failure` entries in `lifecycle:state` retained (real factory behavior).

## 6. Remaining Ambiguities

- `operation_end_time` differs across the 3 rows of an instance (per-row operation end, not a constant); the schema uses the value on the relevant row, which is consistent with the duration convention above.
- `parameters` has 1 missing value (on a `complete` row); kept as-is since it is not a key column.
- 2 instances have only 2 distinct `operation_end_time` values across their rows (negligible; no action taken).

# Column Mapping Report — fischertechnik_lab_B (significant-hilarious-cuscus)

## 1. Dataset Summary

- **Source**: `work_files/eventlog.parquet` → cleaned: `work_files/eventlog_cleaned.parquet`
- **Shape**: 1,383 rows × 20 columns (raw); 1,383 rows × 12 columns (cleaned)
- **Structure**: lifecycle layout — exactly 3 rows per activity instance (`scheduled` → `start` → `complete`), 461 instances, 38 cases (workpieces), 20 activities, 15 resources, 9 process-model variants.
- **Time span**: t0 = 2021-06-30T15:24:34Z, horizon T ≈ 5,943.7 s (~99 min).
- **Outcomes**: 452 success, 9 failure (kept — real factory behavior; HTTP 418/401 on the `complete` row).
- **No duplicate rows**; no missing values in key columns.

## 2. Column Mapping

| Column | Meaning | Simulation Role | Sim-Relevant | Action |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `time:timestamp` | Timestamp of the lifecycle transition (ISO8601, mixed precision) | Request time on `scheduled` row; **service start** on `start` row | Yes | Keep; parse to seconds. Actual duration = `operation_end_time` − `time:timestamp` on `start` rows only |
| `operation_end_time` | Operation end timestamp (ISO8601) | **Service end** (preferred over `time:timestamp` of the `complete` row) | Yes | Keep; parse to seconds |
| `lifecycle:transition` | Transition type: `scheduled` / `start` / `complete` | Lifecycle column | Yes | Keep |
| `lifecycle:state` | `assigned` (scheduled) / `inProgress` (start) / `success` / `failure` (complete) | Outcome column; 9 failures retained | Yes | Keep |
| `event_id` | Integer id shared by the 3 rows of an instance (1002–1483) | Redundant instance key | No | **Drop** (keep `identifier:id`) |
| `identifier:id` | Activity-instance id (e.g. `a_15513`), unique per instance | Instance column linking the 3 lifecycle rows | Yes | Keep |
| `process_model_id` | Process-model / product variant (WF_101…WF_1107), 9 values | Variant column | Yes | Keep |
| `case` | Workpiece id, e.g. `WF_101_13` (prefix = process model, 100% consistent) | Case column | Yes | Keep |
| `concept:name` | Activity name (e.g. `/ov/burn`, `/vgr/pick_up_and_transport`), 20 values | Activity column | Yes | Keep |
| `requested_service_url` | REST URL of the service call; resource query param matches `org:resource` 100% | Redundant (resource already mapped); carries size/thickness for burn | No | **Drop** (parameters carry the same info) |
| `org:resource` | Executing resource (vgr_1/2, hbw_1/2, mm_1/2, ov_1, hw_1, wt_1/2, sm_1, …), 15 values | Resource column | Yes | Keep |
| `planned_operation_time` | Planned duration, timedelta string (e.g. `0 days 00:00:47`) | Planned processing time | Yes | Keep; **parse to seconds** (22 distinct values, 5–222 s) |
| `parameters` | Dict string of activity parameters (positions, hbw slot, burn size/thickness, NFC flag); 1 missing on a `complete` row | Activity parameters (routing/variant detail) | Yes | Keep |
| `case:concept:name` | Identical to `case` (100%) | Redundant | No | **Drop** |
| `SubProcessID` | UUID present only on `start` rows (459/461) | Redundant instance detail | No | **Drop** |
| `current_task` | Free-text task description, only on `start` rows | Redundant narrative | No | **Drop** |
| `response_status_code` | HTTP code on `complete` rows (200 / 418×7 / 401×2) | Redundant with `lifecycle:state` (success↔200, failure↔418/401, 100% consistent) | No | **Drop** |
| `complete_service_time` | Full response time scheduled→complete incl. queueing (timedelta string), only on `complete` rows | Reference metric (mean 73.6 s vs 30.4 s actual service) | Yes | Keep (do not use as service duration) |
| `human_workstation_green_button_pressed` | 1/0 flag, only on `/hw/human_review` instances (87 rows) | Human-intervention detail; not needed for core simulation | No | **Drop** |
| `unsatisfied_condition_description` | Precondition-failure detail (NFC/light-barrier/warehouse errors), only on the 9 failed instances | Diagnostic detail of failures | No | **Drop** |

## 3. Log Schema (confirmed via `set_log_schema`)

- **Layout**: lifecycle — one row per transition; 3 rows per instance.
- **case_col**: `case` | **activity_col**: `concept:name` | **resource_col**: `org:resource` | **variant_col**: `process_model_id`
- **start_col**: `time:timestamp` | **end_col**: `operation_end_time` (preferred over `complete`-row timestamp)
- **lifecycle_col**: `lifecycle:transition` | **instance_col**: `identifier:id`
- **enabled_value**: `scheduled` (queue entry / request) | **start_value**: `start` | **complete_value**: `complete`
- **state_col**: `lifecycle:state` | success: `success` | failure: `failure`
- **Validation**: 461 instances, 38 cases, 20 activities, 15 resources; `enabled_observed_frac = 1.0` (waiting times fully observable); `end_missing = 0`; no warnings. Sample verified: e.g. `/hbw/unload` on `hbw_2`: enabled 0.0 s → start 3.56 s → end 55.91 s (≈ start + 52 s planned).
- **Duration convention**: actual service duration = `operation_end_time − time:timestamp` on `start` rows only (mean 30.4 s, min 0.0, max 218.7 s, no negatives). `complete_service_time` records the full response time (scheduled → complete, incl. queueing; mean 73.6 s, max 1,079 s) and is kept only as a reference metric.

## 4. Excluded Columns

`event_id`, `case:concept:name`, `SubProcessID`, `current_task`, `response_status_code`, `requested_service_url`, `unsatisfied_condition_description`, `human_workstation_green_button_pressed` (8 columns; all redundant or diagnostic-only).

## 5. Cleaning Summary

- Dropped 8 columns (above).
- Drop rows with missing values in key columns (`identifier:id`, `case`, `concept:name`, `org:resource`, `time:timestamp`, `operation_end_time`, `lifecycle:transition`, `lifecycle:state`): **0 rows removed** (no missing values in these columns).
- Duplicate rows: none.
- Result: 1,383 rows × 12 columns → `eventlog_cleaned.parquet`.
- All 9 `failure` entries in `lifecycle:state` retained (real factory behavior).

## 6. Remaining Ambiguities

- `operation_end_time` differs across the 3 rows of an instance (per-row operation end, not a constant); the schema uses the value on the relevant row, which is consistent with the duration convention above.
- `parameters` has 1 missing value (on a `complete` row); kept as-is since it is not a key column.
- 2 instances have only 2 distinct `operation_end_time` values across their rows (negligible; no action taken).

## 1. Dataset Summary

- **Source**: `work_files/eventlog.parquet` → cleaned: `work_files/eventlog_cleaned.parquet`
- **Shape**: 1,383 rows × 20 columns (raw); 1,383 rows × 12 columns (cleaned)
- **Structure**: lifecycle layout — exactly 3 rows per activity instance (`scheduled` → `start` → `complete`), 461 instances, 38 cases (workpieces), 20 activities, 15 resources, 9 process-model variants.
- **Time span**: t0 = 2021-06-30T15:24:34Z, horizon T ≈ 5,943.7 s (~99 min).
- **Outcomes**: 452 success, 9 failure (kept — real factory behavior; HTTP 418/401 on the `complete` row).
- **No duplicate rows**; no missing values in key columns.

## 2. Column Mapping

| Column | Meaning | Simulation Role | Sim-Relevant | Action |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `time:timestamp` | Timestamp of the lifecycle transition (ISO8601, mixed precision) | Request time on `scheduled` row; **service start** on `start` row | Yes | Keep; parse to seconds. Actual duration = `operation_end_time` − `time:timestamp` on `start` rows only |
| `operation_end_time` | Operation end timestamp (ISO8601) | **Service end** (preferred over `time:timestamp` of the `complete` row) | Yes | Keep; parse to seconds |
| `lifecycle:transition` | Transition type: `scheduled` / `start` / `complete` | Lifecycle column | Yes | Keep |
| `lifecycle:state` | `assigned` (scheduled) / `inProgress` (start) / `success` / `failure` (complete) | Outcome column; 9 failures retained | Yes | Keep |
| `event_id` | Integer id shared by the 3 rows of an instance (1002–1483) | Redundant instance key | No | **Drop** (keep `identifier:id`) |
| `identifier:id` | Activity-instance id (e.g. `a_15513`), unique per instance | Instance column linking the 3 lifecycle rows | Yes | Keep |
| `process_model_id` | Process-model / product variant (WF_101…WF_1107), 9 values | Variant column | Yes | Keep |
| `case` | Workpiece id, e.g. `WF_101_13` (prefix = process model, 100% consistent) | Case column | Yes | Keep |
| `concept:name` | Activity name (e.g. `/ov/burn`, `/vgr/pick_up_and_transport`), 20 values | Activity column | Yes | Keep |
| `requested_service_url` | REST URL of the service call; resource query param matches `org:resource` 100% | Redundant (resource already mapped); carries size/thickness for burn | No | **Drop** (parameters carry the same info) |
| `org:resource` | Executing resource (vgr_1/2, hbw_1/2, mm_1/2, ov_1, hw_1, wt_1/2, sm_1, …), 15 values | Resource column | Yes | Keep |
| `planned_operation_time` | Planned duration, timedelta string (e.g. `0 days 00:00:47`) | Planned processing time | Yes | Keep; **parse to seconds** (22 distinct values, 5–222 s) |
| `parameters` | Dict string of activity parameters (positions, hbw slot, burn size/thickness, NFC flag); 1 missing on a `complete` row | Activity parameters (routing/variant detail) | Yes | Keep |
| `case:concept:name` | Identical to `case` (100%) | Redundant | No | **Drop** |
| `SubProcessID` | UUID present only on `start` rows (459/461) | Redundant instance detail | No | **Drop** |
| `current_task` | Free-text task description, only on `start` rows | Redundant narrative | No | **Drop** |
| `response_status_code` | HTTP code on `complete` rows (200 / 418×7 / 401×2) | Redundant with `lifecycle:state` (success↔200, failure↔418/401, 100% consistent) | No | **Drop** |
| `complete_service_time` | Full response time scheduled→complete incl. queueing (timedelta string), only on `complete` rows | Reference metric (mean 73.6 s vs 30.4 s actual service) | Yes | Keep (do not use as service duration) |
| `human_workstation_green_button_pressed` | 1/0 flag, only on `/hw/human_review` instances (87 rows) | Human-intervention detail; not needed for core simulation | No | **Drop** |
| `unsatisfied_condition_description` | Precondition-failure detail (NFC/light-barrier/warehouse errors), only on the 9 failed instances | Diagnostic detail of failures | No | **Drop** |

## 3. Log Schema (confirmed via `set_log_schema`)

- **Layout**: lifecycle — one row per transition; 3 rows per instance.
- **case_col**: `case` | **activity_col**: `concept:name` | **resource_col**: `org:resource` | **variant_col**: `process_model_id`
- **start_col**: `time:timestamp` | **end_col**: `operation_end_time` (preferred over `complete`-row timestamp)
- **lifecycle_col**: `lifecycle:transition` | **instance_col**: `identifier:id`
- **enabled_value**: `scheduled` (queue entry / request) | **start_value**: `start` | **complete_value**: `complete`
- **state_col**: `lifecycle:state` | success: `success` | failure: `failure`
- **Validation**: 461 instances, 38 cases, 20 activities, 15 resources; `enabled_observed_frac = 1.0` (waiting times fully observable); `end_missing = 0`; no warnings. Sample verified: e.g. `/hbw/unload` on `hbw_2`: enabled 0.0 s → start 3.56 s → end 55.91 s (≈ start + 52 s planned).
- **Duration convention**: actual service duration = `operation_end_time − time:timestamp` on `start` rows only (mean 30.4 s, min 0.0, max 218.7 s, no negatives). `complete_service_time` records the full response time (scheduled → complete, incl. queueing; mean 73.6 s, max 1,079 s) and is kept only as a reference metric.

## 4. Excluded Columns

`event_id`, `case:concept:name`, `SubProcessID`, `current_task`, `response_status_code`, `requested_service_url`, `unsatisfied_condition_description`, `human_workstation_green_button_pressed` (8 columns; all redundant or diagnostic-only).

## 5. Cleaning Summary

- Dropped 8 columns (above).
- Drop rows with missing values in key columns (`identifier:id`, `case`, `concept:name`, `org:resource`, `time:timestamp`, `operation_end_time`, `lifecycle:transition`, `lifecycle:state`): **0 rows removed** (no missing values in these columns).
- Duplicate rows: none.
- Result: 1,383 rows × 12 columns → `eventlog_cleaned.parquet`.
- All 9 `failure` entries in `lifecycle:state` retained (real factory behavior).

## 6. Remaining Ambiguities

- `operation_end_time` differs across the 3 rows of an instance (per-row operation end, not a constant); the schema uses the value on the relevant row, which is consistent with the duration convention above.
- `parameters` has 1 missing value (on a `complete` row); kept as-is since it is not a key column.
- 2 instances have only 2 distinct `operation_end_time` values across their rows (negligible; no action taken).

import pandas as pd
path = "/beegfs2/scratch/rreider/genai4simpy/output/fischertechnik_lab_B/significant-hilarious-cuscus/work_files/eventlog_cleaned.parquet"
df = pd.read_parquet(path)

inst = df[df["lifecycle:transition"] == "start"].copy()
inst["t_start"] = pd.to_datetime(inst["time:timestamp"], format="mixed").astype("int64") / 1e9
inst["t_end"] = pd.to_datetime(inst["operation_end_time"], format="mixed").astype("int64") / 1e9
comp = df[df["lifecycle:transition"] == "complete"][["identifier:id", "lifecycle:state"]].rename(columns={"lifecycle:state": "state"})
inst = inst.merge(comp, on="identifier:id", how="left")
inst["dur"] = inst["t_end"] - inst["t_start"]

t0 = pd.Timestamp("2021-06-30 15:24:34.013477+00:00").value / 1e9
rows = []
for case, g in inst.sort_values("t_start").groupby("case"):
    g = g.sort_values("t_start")
    seq = list(g["concept:name"])
    rows.append({
        "case": case, "variant": g["process_model_id"].iloc[0], "n": len(g),
        "first_t": round(g["t_start"].min() - t0, 1), "last_t": round(g["t_end"].max() - t0, 1),
        "last_state": g.iloc[-1]["state"], "n_fail": int((g["state"] == "failure").sum()),
        "seq": " -> ".join(seq),
    })
out = pd.DataFrame(rows).sort_values("case")
pd.set_option("display.width", 400); pd.set_option("display.max_colwidth", 400)
print(out.to_string(index=False))

# failures: which instances failed and what happened after
print("\nFAILED INSTANCES:")
fail = df[df["lifecycle:state"] == "failure"]
print(fail[["case", "concept:name", "org:resource", "identifier:id"]].to_string(index=False))

import pandas as pd
path = "/beegfs2/scratch/rreider/genai4simpy/output/fischertechnik_lab_B/significant-hilarious-cuscus/work_files/eventlog_cleaned.parquet"
df = pd.read_parquet(path)

inst = df[df["lifecycle:transition"] == "start"].copy()
inst["t_start"] = pd.to_datetime(inst["time:timestamp"], format="mixed").astype("int64") / 1e6
inst["t_end"] = pd.to_datetime(inst["operation_end_time"], format="mixed").astype("int64") / 1e6
comp = df[df["lifecycle:transition"] == "complete"][["identifier:id", "lifecycle:state"]].rename(columns={"lifecycle:state": "state"})
inst = inst.merge(comp, on="identifier:id", how="left")
inst["dur"] = inst["t_end"] - inst["t_start"]

t0 = pd.Timestamp("2021-06-30 15:24:34.013477+00:00").value / 1e6
rows = []
for case, g in inst.sort_values("t_start").groupby("case"):
    g = g.sort_values("t_start")
    rows.append({
        "case": case, "variant": g["process_model_id"].iloc[0], "n": len(g),
        "first_t": round(g["t_start"].min() - t0, 1), "last_t": round(g["t_end"].max() - t0, 1),
        "last_state": g.iloc[-1]["state"], "n_fail": int((g["state"] == "failure").sum()),
        "seq": " -> ".join(g["concept:name"]),
    })
out = pd.DataFrame(rows).sort_values("case")
pd.set_option("display.width", 400); pd.set_option("display.max_colwidth", 400)
print(out.to_string(index=False))
out.to_csv("/beegfs2/scratch/rreider/genai4simpy/output/fischertechnik_lab_B/significant-hilarious-cuscus/work_files/case_summary.csv", index=False)

inst = df[df["lifecycle:transition"] == "start"].copy()
inst["t_start"] = pd.to_datetime(inst["time:timestamp"], format="mixed").astype("int64") / 1e6
inst["t_end"] = pd.to_datetime(inst["operation_end_time"], format="mixed").astype("int64") / 1e6
comp = df[df["lifecycle:transition"] == "complete"][["identifier:id", "lifecycle:state"]].rename(columns={"lifecycle:state": "state"})
inst = inst.merge(comp, on="identifier:id", how="left")
inst["dur"] = inst["t_end"] - inst["t_start"]

t0 = pd.Timestamp("2021-06-30 15:24:34.013477+00:00").value / 1e6
rows = []
for case, g in inst.sort_values("t_start").groupby("case"):
    g = g.sort_values("t_start")

        "first_t": round(g["t_start"].min() - t0, 1), "last_t": round(g["t_end"].max() - t0, 1),

        "seq": " -> ".join(g["concept:name"]),
    })
out = pd.DataFrame(rows).sort_values("case")
pd.set_option("display.width", 400); pd.set_option("display.max_colwidth", 400)
print(out.to_string(index=False))
out.to_csv("/beegfs2/scratch/rreider/genai4simpy/output/fischertechnik_lab_B/significant-hilarious-cuscus/work_files/case_summary.csv", index=False)

path = "/beegfs2/scratch/rreider/genai4simpy/output/fischertechnik_lab_B/significant-hilarious-cuscus/work_files/eventlog_cleaned.parquet"

# instance-level (start rows) with resource + state
inst = df[df["lifecycle:transition"] == "start"].copy()
inst["t"] = pd.to_datetime(inst["time:timestamp"], format="mixed").astype("int64") / 1e6
comp = df[df["lifecycle:transition"] == "complete"][["identifier:id","lifecycle:state"]].rename(columns={"lifecycle:state":"state"})
inst = inst.merge(comp, on="identifier:id", how="left")

TERMINAL = "/hw/human_review"
EXCLUDED = {"WF_102_16","WF_102_17","WF_104_9"}  # terminate immediately after failure, no recovery

cases = {}
for case, g in inst.sort_values("t").groupby("case"):
    g = g.sort_values("t")
    steps = list(zip(g["concept:name"], g["org:resource"]))
    states = list(g["state"])
    cases[case] = {
        "variant": g["process_model_id"].iloc[0],
        "steps": steps,
        "last_state": states[-1],
        "reaches_terminal": TERMINAL in [a for a,_ in steps],
        "n_steps": len(steps),
    }

# capacity check: any two instances on same resource overlapping in time?
inst2 = inst.copy()
inst2["t_end"] = pd.to_datetime(inst2["operation_end_time"], format="mixed").astype("int64")/1e6
max_overlap = {}
for res, g in inst2.groupby("org:resource"):
    g = g.sort_values("t")
    ov = 0
    for i in range(len(g)):
        for j in range(i+1, len(g)):
            if g["t"].iloc[j] < g["t_end"].iloc[i]:
                ov += 1
    if ov: max_overlap[res] = ov
print("SAME-RESOURCE OVERLAPS (should be empty for capacity 1):", max_overlap if max_overlap else "NONE")

# per-variant routing subtypes (completed cases only) + early exits
print("\n=== ROUTING SUBTYPES (completed cases) ===")
result = {}
for v in sorted(set(c["variant"] for c in cases.values())):
    vc = [c for c in cases.values() if c["variant"]==v]
    N = len(vc)
    completed = [c for c in vc if c["reaches_terminal"] and c["case"] not in EXCLUDED]
    # note: case key
    completed = [c for c in completed]
    early = [c for c in vc if (not c["reaches_terminal"]) and c["last_state"]=="success" and c["case"] not in EXCLUDED]
    excl  = [c for c in vc if c["case"] in EXCLUDED]
    # group completed by exact sequence
    seqs = OrderedDict()
    for c in completed:
        key = tuple(a for a,_ in c["steps"])
        seqs.setdefault(key, []).append(c)
    result[v] = {"N":N, "n_completed":len(completed), "n_early":len(early), "n_excluded":len(excl),
                 "early_exit_prob": round(len(early)/N,4),
                 "early_points": {f"{c['steps'][-1][0]} (success)": c["n_steps"] for c in early},
                 "excluded": [c["case"] for c in excl],
                 "seqs": []}
    for key, cs in seqs.items():
        # resources_by_step: for each position, the resource distribution across these cases
        rbs = []
        for pos in range(len(key)):
            rc = Counter(c["steps"][pos][1] for c in cs)
            tot = sum(rc.values())
            rbs.append(OrderedDict((r, round(n/tot,3)) for r,n in rc.most_common()))
        result[v]["seqs"].append({"seq": list(key), "n": len(cs), "prob_of_completed": round(len(cs)/len(completed),4),
                                  "resources_by_step": rbs})
print(json.dumps(result, indent=1))

## 3. Log Schema (confirmed via `set_log_schema`)

- **Layout**: lifecycle — one row per transition; 3 rows per instance.
- **case_col**: `case` | **activity_col**: `concept:name` | **resource_col**: `org:resource` | **variant_col**: `process_model_id`
- **start_col**: `time:timestamp` | **end_col**: `operation_end_time` (preferred over `complete`-row timestamp)
- **lifecycle_col**: `lifecycle:transition` | **instance_col**: `identifier:id`
- **enabled_value**: `scheduled` (queue entry / request) | **start_value**: `start` | **complete_value**: `complete`
- **state_col**: `lifecycle:state` | success: `success` | failure: `failure`
- **Validation**: 461 instances, 38 cases, 20 activities, 15 resources; `enabled_observed_frac = 1.0` (waiting times fully observable); `end_missing = 0`; no warnings. Sample verified: e.g. `/hbw/unload` on `hbw_2`: enabled 0.0 s → start 3.56 s → end 55.91 s (≈ start + 52 s planned).
- **Duration convention**: actual service duration = `operation_end_time − time:timestamp` on `start` rows only (mean 30.4 s, min 0.0, max 218.7 s, no negatives). `complete_service_time` records the full response time (scheduled → complete, incl. queueing; mean 73.6 s, max 1,079 s) and is kept only as a reference metric.

## 4. Excluded Columns

`event_id`, `case:concept:name`, `SubProcessID`, `current_task`, `response_status_code`, `requested_service_url`, `unsatisfied_condition_description`, `human_workstation_green_button_pressed` (8 columns; all redundant or diagnostic-only).

## 5. Cleaning Summary

- Dropped 8 columns (above).
- Drop rows with missing values in key columns (`identifier:id`, `case`, `concept:name`, `org:resource`, `time:timestamp`, `operation_end_time`, `lifecycle:transition`, `lifecycle:state`): **0 rows removed** (no missing values in these columns).
- Duplicate rows: none.
- Result: 1,383 rows × 12 columns → `eventlog_cleaned.parquet`.
- All 9 `failure` entries in `lifecycle:state` retained (real factory behavior).

## 6. Remaining Ambiguities

- `operation_end_time` differs across the 3 rows of an instance (per-row operation end, not a constant); the schema uses the value on the relevant row, which is consistent with the duration convention above.
- `parameters` has 1 missing value (on a `complete` row); kept as-is since it is not a key column.
- 2 instances have only 2 distinct `operation_end_time` values across their rows (negligible; no action taken).

## 1. Dataset Summary

- **Source**: `work_files/eventlog.parquet` → cleaned: `work_files/eventlog_cleaned.parquet`

- **Structure**: lifecycle layout — exactly 3 rows per activity instance (`scheduled` → `start` → `complete`), 461 instances, 38 cases (workpieces), 20 activities, 15 resources, 9 process-model variants.

- **No duplicate rows**; no missing values in key columns.

| `lifecycle:state` | `assigned` (scheduled) / `inProgress` (start) / `success` / `failure` (complete) | Outcome column; 9 failures retained | Yes | Keep |

| `process_model_id` | Process-model / product variant (WF_101…WF_1107), 9 values | Variant column | Yes | Keep |
| `case` | Workpiece id, e.g. `WF_101_13` (prefix = process model, 100% consistent) | Case column | Yes | Keep |
| `concept:name` | Activity name (e.g. `/ov/burn`, `/vgr/pick_up_and_transport`), 20 values | Activity column | Yes | Keep |

| `org:resource` | Executing resource (vgr_1/2, hbw_1/2, mm_1/2, ov_1, hw_1, wt_1/2, sm_1, …), 15 values | Resource column | Yes | Keep |

## 3. Log Schema (confirmed via `set_log_schema`)

- **Layout**: lifecycle — one row per transition; 3 rows per instance.
- **case_col**: `case` | **activity_col**: `concept:name` | **resource_col**: `org:resource` | **variant_col**: `process_model_id`
- **start_col**: `time:timestamp` | **end_col**: `operation_end_time` (preferred over `complete`-row timestamp)
- **lifecycle_col**: `lifecycle:transition` | **instance_col**: `identifier:id`
- **enabled_value**: `scheduled` (queue entry / request) | **start_value**: `start` | **complete_value**: `complete`
- **state_col**: `lifecycle:state` | success: `success` | failure: `failure`
- **Validation**: 461 instances, 38 cases, 20 activities, 15 resources; `enabled_observed_frac = 1.0` (waiting times fully observable); `end_missing = 0`; no warnings. Sample verified: e.g. `/hbw/unload` on `hbw_2`: enabled 0.0 s → start 3.56 s → end 55.91 s (≈ start + 52 s planned).
- **Duration convention**: actual service duration = `operation_end_time − time:timestamp` on `start` rows only (mean 30.4 s, min 0.0, max 218.7 s, no negatives). `complete_service_time` records the full response time (scheduled → complete, incl. queueing; mean 73.6 s, max 1,079 s) and is kept only as a reference metric.

## 4. Excluded Columns

`event_id`, `case:concept:name`, `SubProcessID`, `current_task`, `response_status_code`, `requested_service_url`, `unsatisfied_condition_description`, `human_workstation_green_button_pressed` (8 columns; all redundant or diagnostic-only).

## 5. Cleaning Summary

- Dropped 8 columns (above).
- Drop rows with missing values in key columns (`identifier:id`, `case`, `concept:name`, `org:resource`, `time:timestamp`, `operation_end_time`, `lifecycle:transition`, `lifecycle:state`): **0 rows removed** (no missing values in these columns).
- Duplicate rows: none.
- Result: 1,383 rows × 12 columns → `eventlog_cleaned.parquet`.
- All 9 `failure` entries in `lifecycle:state` retained (real factory behavior).

## 6. Remaining Ambiguities

- `operation_end_time` differs across the 3 rows of an instance (per-row operation end, not a constant); the schema uses the value on the relevant row, which is consistent with the duration convention above.
- `parameters` has 1 missing value (on a `complete` row); kept as-is since it is not a key column.
- 2 instances have only 2 distinct `operation_end_time` values across their rows (negligible; no action taken).

## 3. Log Schema (confirmed via `set_log_schema`)

- **Layout**: lifecycle — one row per transition; 3 rows per instance.
- **case_col**: `case` | **activity_col**: `concept:name` | **resource_col**: `org:resource` | **variant_col**: `process_model_id`
- **start_col**: `time:timestamp` | **end_col**: `operation_end_time` (preferred over `complete`-row timestamp)
- **lifecycle_col**: `lifecycle:transition` | **instance_col**: `identifier:id`
- **enabled_value**: `scheduled` (queue entry / request) | **start_value**: `start` | **complete_value**: `complete`
- **state_col**: `lifecycle:state` | success: `success` | failure: `failure`
- **Validation**: 461 instances, 38 cases, 20 activities, 15 resources; `enabled_observed_frac = 1.0` (waiting times fully observable); `end_missing = 0`; no warnings. Sample verified: e.g. `/hbw/unload` on `hbw_2`: enabled 0.0 s → start 3.56 s → end 55.91 s (≈ start + 52 s planned).
- **Duration convention**: actual service duration = `operation_end_time − time:timestamp` on `start` rows only (mean 30.4 s, min 0.0, max 218.7 s, no negatives). `complete_service_time` records the full response time (scheduled → complete, incl. queueing; mean 73.6 s, max 1,079 s) and is kept only as a reference metric.

## 4. Excluded Columns

`event_id`, `case:concept:name`, `SubProcessID`, `current_task`, `response_status_code`, `requested_service_url`, `unsatisfied_condition_description`, `human_workstation_green_button_pressed` (8 columns; all redundant or diagnostic-only).

## 5. Cleaning Summary

- Dropped 8 columns (above).
- Drop rows with missing values in key columns (`identifier:id`, `case`, `concept:name`, `org:resource`, `time:timestamp`, `operation_end_time`, `lifecycle:transition`, `lifecycle:state`): **0 rows removed** (no missing values in these columns).
- Duplicate rows: none.
- Result: 1,383 rows × 12 columns → `eventlog_cleaned.parquet`.
- All 9 `failure` entries in `lifecycle:state` retained (real factory behavior).

## 6. Remaining Ambiguities

- `operation_end_time` differs across the 3 rows of an instance (per-row operation end, not a constant); the schema uses the value on the relevant row, which is consistent with the duration convention above.
- `parameters` has 1 missing value (on a `complete` row); kept as-is since it is not a key column.
- 2 instances have only 2 distinct `operation_end_time` values across their rows (negligible; no action taken).

print('ACTIVITIES IN DATA:', sorted(inst['concept:name'].unique()))

# For each case: check overlap between adjacent steps (prev end > next start)

for res, g in st.groupby('org:resource'):
    iv = list(zip(g['t0'], g['t1']))
    pts = sorted([a for a,_ in iv] + [b for _,b in iv])
    mx = 0
    for p in pts:
        c = sum(1 for a,b in iv if a <= p <= b)
        mx = max(mx, c)
    print(f"  {res:6s} n={len(g):3d} max_concurrent={mx}")

print("\n=== per-variant overlapping consecutive pairs (overlap>0.5s) ===")
ov = defaultdict(list)
for case, g in st.groupby('case'):
    rows = g.to_dict('records')
    var = rows[0]['process_model_id']
    for i in range(1, len(rows)):
        a, b = rows[i-1], rows[i]
        o = (min(a['t1'], b['t1']) - max(a['t0'], b['t0'])).total_seconds()
        if o > 0.5:
            ov[(var, a['concept:name'], b['concept:name'])].append(o)

# Topology Report — fischertechnik_lab_B (significant-hilarious-cuscus)

## 1. Scope & Data Basis

- **Source**: `work_files/eventlog_cleaned.parquet` (1,383 rows × 12 cols; lifecycle layout, 3 rows per instance).
- **Volume**: 461 activity instances, 38 cases (workpieces), 20 activities, 15 resources, 9 process-model variants.
- **Window**: t0 = 2021-06-30T15:24:34Z, horizon ≈ 5,943.7 s (~99 min).
- **Outcomes**: 452 success, 9 failure (real factory behavior, retained).

## 2. Censoring & Case Classification (detect_censoring)

| Category | Count | Cases |
|---|---|---|
| Complete (end with `/hbw/store`) | 14 | WF_101_14, WF_101_18, WF_102_15, WF_102_18, WF_104_11, WF_104_8, WF_105_8, WF_105_9, WF_108_7, WF_108_9, WF_1106_7, WF_1106_8, WF_1107_6, WF_1107_7 |
| Right-censored (cut at window end) | 0 | — |
| Left-censored / initial WIP | 0 | — |
| Incomplete interior (early exit) | 24 | see §7 |

- No case overlaps the window edges (edge_tol 72.2 s); **no window truncation** — all 24 incomplete cases are genuine mid-process stops (early exits / scrap / abandonment), not truncation.
- Initial WIP at window start = 0 → simulation starts empty.
- **Excluded as truncation artifacts** (terminate immediately after a failure, no recovery): **WF_102_16** (ends in failed `/vgr/pick_up_and_transport`), **WF_102_17** (single failed `/hbw/unload`), **WF_104_9** (single failed `/hbw/unload`). Per project decision, only these are excluded; all other failed steps are real retry behavior.
- Estimation basis: main sequences & step presence from **complete cases**; early-exit statistics from non-excluded cases; variant mix from all 38 released cases.

## 3. Resources (15, all capacity 1 — verified, max concurrent service per resource = 1)

| Resource | Class | Capacity | Instances | Role |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| hbw_1 | hbw | 1 | 30 | warehouse: get_empty_bucket, store |
| hbw_2 | hbw | 1 | 74 | warehouse: unload, store_empty_bucket |
| vgr_1 | vgr | 1 | 85 | vertical gripper (in-process transport) |
| vgr_2 | vgr | 1 | 42 | vertical gripper (initial pick-up) |
| wt_1 | wt | 1 | 27 | workpiece transport |
| wt_2 | wt | 1 | 14 | workpiece transport |
| mm_1 | mm | 1 | 37 | milling (mill, deburr, transport_from_to) |
| mm_2 | mm | 1 | 17 | milling (mill, drill, deburr) |
| ov_1 | ov | 1 | 35 | oven (burn, temper) |
| ov_2 | ov | 1 | 12 | oven (burn) |
| sm_1 | sm | 1 | 23 | sorting/transport |
| sm_2 | sm | 1 | 14 | sorting/transport |
| pm_1 | pm | 1 | 13 | press (punch_gill, punch_recesses, punch_ribbing) |
| dm_2 | dm | 1 | 8 | deep milling (lower, cylindrical_drill) |
| hw_1 | hw | 1 | 30 | human review workstation |

## 4. Variant Routing (9 variants; all observed sub-types captured)

Variant mix (share of 38 released cases): WF_101 0.158, WF_102 0.132, WF_103 0.132, WF_104 0.132, WF_105 0.105, WF_108 0.079, WF_109 0.105, WF_1106 0.105, WF_1107 0.053.

All variants share the skeleton: `/hbw/unload` (hbw_2) → `/vgr/pick_up_and_transport` (vgr_2) → [optional `/hbw/store_empty_bucket` (hbw_2)] → process steps → `/hw/human_review` (hw_1) → [optional `/hbw/get_empty_bucket` (hbw_1) → `/vgr/pick_up_and_transport` (vgr_1) → `/hbw/store` (hbw_1)].

| Variant | n cases | completed | Main sequence (complete cases) | Early exit P | Early-exit points |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| WF_101 | 6 | 2 | U → V2 → SEB → V1 → B(ov_1) → T(ov_1) → W1 → M1 → D1 → SO1 → V1 → H → GEB → V1 → V1 → S | 0.667 | after H (0.75), after V1 (0.25) |
| WF_102 | 5 | 2 | U → V2 → SEB → B(ov_2) → W2 → DR2 → ST2 → L2 → V1 → H → V1 → GEB → V1 → S | 0.333 | after H (1.0, of non-excluded) |
| WF_103 | 5 | 0 | U → V2 → SEB → V1 → B(ov_1) → T(ov_1) → W1 → M1 → D1 → ST1 → PR1 → V1 → H (partial, no complete case) | 1.0 | after B (0.2), after H (0.8) |
| WF_104 | 5 | 2 | U → V2 → SEB → B(ov_2) → W2 → M2 → SO2 → V2 → V1 → W1 → D1 → ST1 → PG1 → V1 → H → V1 → GEB → V1 → S | 0.5 | after B (0.5), after H (0.5) |

| WF_1106 | 4 | 2 | U → V2 → SEB → B(ov_2) → W2 → M2/MT2 → ST2 → CD2 → V1 → H → GEB → V1 → V1 → S | 0.5 | after H (0.5), after CD2 (0.5) |
| WF_1107 | 2 | 2 | U → V2 → SEB → V1 → B(ov_1) → W1 → MT1/PB1 → ST1 → PB1/PR1 → V1 → H → GEB → V1 → V1 → S | 0.0 | — |

(U=unload, V=vgr/pick_up_and_transport, SEB=store_empty_bucket, GEB=get_empty_bucket, S=store, B=burn, T=temper, W=wt/pick_up_and_transport, M=mill, D=deburr, DR=drill, MT=mm/transport_from_to, SO=sort, ST=sm/transport, PR=punch_recesses, PB=punch_ribbing, PG=punch_gill, L=dm/lower, CD=dm/cylindrical_drill, H=human_review; suffix = resource index.)

**Non-canonical sub-sequences captured** (per decision: capture ALL observed variants):
- **WF_102**: WF_102_14 (early exit after H) ran without `/ov/burn` and with an extra `/hbw/store_empty_bucket` on **hbw_1** (concurrent with vgr_1 transport) before human review — captured as `other_sequences` (p=0.333 over non-excluded cases).
- **WF_108**: WF_108_8 (early exit after H) ran without `/ov/burn` — captured as `other_sequences` (p=0.333).
- **WF_1106**: WF_1106_8 used `/mm/transport_from_to` (mm_2) instead of `/mm/mill` — captured as `other_sequences` (p=0.5).
- **WF_1107**: WF_1107_7 used `/mm/mill` + `/pm/punch_recesses` instead of `/mm/transport_from_to` + `/pm/punch_ribbing` — captured as `other_sequences` (p=0.5).

**Storage steps** (`store_empty_bucket` at start; `get_empty_bucket` → `store` at end): conditional/optional but present in **all complete cases** of their variants — captured in the canonical sequence; the absence in incomplete cases is truncation bias, not optionality (step_presence_complete_cases = 1.0).

## 5. Queue Disciplines (test_dispatching_rules, 87 decision points)

| Class | n decisions | FIFO | LIFO | case_age | activity_priority | Best | FIFO rejected? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| hbw | 66 | 0.50 | 0.50 | **0.985** | 0.97 | case_age | **yes** |
| vgr | 21 | **1.00** | 0.00 | 0.476 | 1.00 | FIFO | no |
| all others | — | — | — | — | — | — | no contention at all (100% extraneous waiting) |

- **hbw**: NOT FIFO. Learned activity priority: `/hbw/store` > `/hbw/get_empty_bucket` > `/hbw/store_empty_bucket` > `/hbw/unload`. Dominant overtaking: `store_empty_bucket` chosen over waiting `unload` (110 overtakes). → Model with `simpy.PriorityResource`.
- **vgr**: FIFO consistent (100%).
- All other classes (dm, hw, mm, ov, pm, sm, wt): zero contention waiting — effectively no queue; FIFO.

## 6. Waiting-Time Causes (decompose_waiting_times, 461 steps)

Overall mean wait 41.0 s (p90 66.6 s); shares: contention 29.5%, prioritization 22.6%, extraneous 47.9%.

- **hbw** (104 steps, mean 144.8 s, p90 525.3 s): 28.3% of waiting is overtaking by later-enabled steps → confirms non-FIFO priority queue; `/hbw/unload` alone has mean wait 385.6 s (p90 700 s) because it has the lowest priority.
- **vgr** (127 steps, mean 23.0 s): 49.5% contention (FIFO queueing), 50.5% extraneous (hand-off/transport delay).
- **ov, wt, mm, sm, pm, dm, hw**: 100% extraneous — waiting happens while the resource is idle (hand-off/release delay, not resource capacity).

## 7. Early Exits (24 interior incomplete cases — real scrap/abandonment, not truncation)

| Variant | Exits | After (success) | After (failure) |
|---|---|---|---|
| WF_101 | 4 | /hw/human_review ×3, /vgr/pick_up_and_transport ×1 | — |
| WF_102 | 2 (of 5; 2 excluded) | /hw/human_review ×1 | /vgr/pick_up_and_transport ×1 (WF_102_16, excluded), /hbw/unload ×1 (WF_102_17, excluded) |
| WF_103 | 5 | /ov/burn ×1, /hw/human_review ×4 | — |
| WF_104 | 3 (of 5; 1 excluded) | /ov/burn ×1, /hw/human_review ×1 | /hbw/unload ×1 (WF_104_9, excluded) |
| WF_105 | 2 | /sm/sort ×2 | — |
| WF_108 | 1 | /hw/human_review ×1 | — |
| WF_109 | 4 | /hw/human_review ×4 | — |
| WF_1106 | 2 | /hw/human_review ×1, /dm/cylindrical_drill ×1 | — |
| WF_1107 | 0 | — | — |

Most exits occur at/after `/hw/human_review` (workpiece rejected at inspection) — consistent with scrap at the quality gate.

## 8. Release Control (detect_release_control, 38 releases)

- **Verdict: open (bursty releases)** — no WIP cap (WIP at release: mean 5.0, max 8, no ceiling pattern) and no completion trigger (within-5s lift 0.86 < 1; within-30s lift 1.39, weak).
- Max WIP 9, time-averaged WIP 5.91 (15.2% of time at max).
- **Two-regime arrival process**: 14 bursts (mean size 2.7, up to 9) spaced by burst IAT (mean 2.44 s, median 1.44 s), separated by gaps (mean 394.7 s, median 294.1 s; gap:burst IAT ratio 161.5). Model with a gap process + burst size — never the mixed mean IAT (140.3 s, cv 2.0).

## 9. Intra-Case Concurrency (detect_intra_case_concurrency)

0.974 overlapping steps per case; 68.4% of cases have overlap; 1.571 per completed case → **the process is not a strictly sequential chain**. Material overlapping (previous → next) pairs, physically plausible (transporter fetched / bucket handled while machine still works):

| Pair | n | mean overlap |
|---|---|---|
| /hbw/store_empty_bucket → /ov/burn | 12 | 34.5 s |
| /hbw/store_empty_bucket → /vgr/pick_up_and_transport | 11 | 25.3 s |
| /hbw/get_empty_bucket → /vgr/pick_up_and_transport | 6 | 31.4 s |
| /vgr/pick_up_and_transport → /hbw/get_empty_bucket | 5 | 20.7 s |
| /hbw/store_empty_bucket → /wt/pick_up_and_transport | 3 | 21.7 s |

Modeled via `concurrent_with_previous: true` flags per variant step (e.g. burn starts while store_empty_bucket still runs; vgr fetch starts while get_empty_bucket still runs).

## 10. Failure / Rework Behavior (9 failed instances)

- **Retries on same resource (model as retry-on-same-resource with delay)**: `/wt/pick_up_and_transport` on wt_1 in WF_104_8 (2 consecutive failures → success), WF_109_6, WF_1107_7; `/hbw/store_empty_bucket` on hbw_2 in WF_102_15 and WF_104_8 (failed, case continued — no retry instance, treated as a transient fault absorbed by the process).
- **Terminal failures (truncation artifacts, excluded)**: WF_102_16 (vgr), WF_102_17 (hbw unload), WF_104_9 (hbw unload) — no subsequent activity for the case.

## 11. Control-Logic Summary (written to spec `control_policies`)

- `queue_discipline`: hbw = **priority** (order: store > get_empty_bucket > store_empty_bucket > unload); vgr = fifo; all others fifo (no contention).
- `release_rule`: open (bursty releases) — two-regime burst/gap arrival process.
- `intra_case_concurrency`: the five pairs above.
- `evidence`: hbw FIFO agreement 0.50 (case_age 0.985, activity_priority 0.97 over 66 decisions); vgr FIFO 1.00 (21 decisions); 1.571 overlapping steps per completed case (68.4% of cases).

## 12. Spec Corrections Made During Verification

1. **WF_102 main_sequence** corrected: `/hbw/store_empty_bucket` (hbw_2) is present in **all** WF_102 cases (including both complete cases) — it was missing from the previous main sequence; added as step 3 with `/ov/burn` concurrent.
2. **WF_102 / WF_104 early-exit statistics** recomputed excluding the 3 failure-terminated truncation artifacts (WF_102_16, WF_102_17, WF_104_9) per project decision; their "early exit after step 0 / unload-failure" entries were truncation, not real exits.
3. **WF_102 / WF_108 `other_sequences`** added (non-canonical sub-types: no-burn routing with extra hbw_1 store_empty_bucket; no-burn routing).
4. **`concurrent_with_previous` flags** corrected from raw overlap check: WF_102 `get_empty_bucket`→`vgr` = false (no overlap observed); WF_104 `get_empty_bucket`→`vgr` = false; WF_108 `get_empty_bucket`→`vgr` = true (6.5 s overlap).
5. **`initial_state.excluded_from_estimation`** populated with the 3 truncation-artifact case ids (exclusion list only — not used as model inputs).
6. **`assumptions`** section written (10 entries) recording all modelling decisions and their evidence.
7. **`control_policies.evidence`** completed with case_age/activity_priority agreement rates and overlap statistics.

## 13. Open Questions

See QUESTIONS FOR USER in the final message.

## 8. Release Control (detect_release_control, 38 releases)

- **Verdict: open (bursty releases)** — no WIP cap (WIP at release: mean 5.0, max 8, no ceiling pattern) and no completion trigger (within-5s lift 0.86 < 1; within-30s lift 1.39, weak).

# Extraction Plan Report — fischertechnik_lab_B (significant-hilarious-cuscus)

## 1. Scope & Data Basis

- **Data**: cleaned event log — 1,383 rows, 461 activity instances, 38 cases (workpieces), 20 activities, 15 resources (all capacity 1), 9 process-model variants, window ≈ 5,944 s (~99 min).
- **Duration convention**: actual service duration = end − start taken on the `start` row only (mean 30.4 s, min 0.0 s, max 218.7 s). `complete_service_time` (scheduled→complete, incl. queueing; mean 73.6 s) is a reference metric only — **never** used as service duration.
- **Censoring**: none for durations (end_missing = 0; every instance has a complete row). The 24 early-exit cases stop *after* a completed activity, so no censored service times.
- **Excluded cases** (truncation artifacts — terminal failure, no recovery): WF_102_16, WF_102_17, WF_104_9. Excluded from failure-probability and routing estimation; **included in arrival estimation** (their releases are real system inputs).

## 2. Agent Deployment Recommendation

| Sub-Agent | Deploy? | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| durations-processing-times-agent | **Yes** | 461 instances with full start/end pairs; service times per activity-resource, planned durations, and failure/retry parameters all extractable. |
| inter-arrival-times-agent | **Yes** | 38 releases under open (bursty) release control; two-regime gap/burst process must be extracted and fit. |
| quantities-quality-agent | **No** | No quantity or quality columns exist in the log (no batch sizes, defect counts, or inspection-result columns). Scrap/quality-gate behavior is already captured by the topology's early-exit statistics. |
| distribution-fitting-agent | **Yes** | Distribution review is always required: service times, arrival gaps, burst sizes, within-burst IAT, and retry delays all need fitted distributions with goodness-of-fit checks. |

## 3. Extraction Plan per Agent

### 3.1 durations-processing-times-agent

**A. Actual service times**
- Source: `start` rows only; duration = end − start.
- **Grouping strategy**: start at **activity × resource** level. For high-volume activities, test whether duration genuinely differs across resources and **split only where the difference is real and measurable**; otherwise pool to activity level. High-volume activities to check:
  - `/vgr/pick_up_and_transport` (127 instances; vgr_1 = in-process transport vs vgr_2 = initial pick-up — different roles, likely different durations),
  - `/ov/burn` (ov_1 vs ov_2 — different ovens; burn size/thickness parameters differ),
  - `/mm/mill` (mm_1 vs mm_2),
  - `/wt/pick_up_and_transport` (wt_1 vs wt_2),
  - `/hbw/store_empty_bucket` (hbw_2 only — no split possible).
- **Low-sample combos (n < 10)**: pool within resource class (e.g. mm_1+mm_2, ov_1+ov_2, wt_1+wt_2, sm_1+sm_2, vgr_1+vgr_2, hbw_1+hbw_2) rather than estimating per-resource.
- **Successful vs. failed instances**: build the service-time distribution from the 452 successful instances; record the 9 failed attempts' durations separately (failed attempts may run differently and feed the failure/retry model, not the nominal service distribution).
- **Data notes**: min duration is 0.0 s — flag zero/near-zero instances (possible instantaneous hand-off steps) before fitting; `/hw/human_review` (30 instances) is human-driven and expected to be high-variance.

**B. Planned durations (separate set)**
- Parse `planned_operation_time` (22 distinct values, 5–222 s) per activity as a **separate planned-duration set** for comparison/validation against actuals (ratio actual/planned per activity; flag activities where actuals systematically deviate from plan).

**C. Failure & retry parameters (explicit — do not defer to manual modeling)**
- **Failure probability per activity × resource**: failed instances / total instances, estimated from the 6 retryable failures only (the 3 excluded terminal failures are truncation artifacts and are **not** used for failure-rate estimation):
  - `/wt/pick_up_and_transport` on wt_1: 4 failed attempts (WF_104_8 ×2 consecutive, WF_109_6, WF_1107_7),
  - `/hbw/store_empty_bucket` on hbw_2: 2 failed attempts (WF_102_15, WF_104_8) — **no retry instance** (transient fault absorbed; case continued) → model as failure-without-retry.
- **Retry delay**: for each retryable failure, delay = start of the retry instance − complete of the failed instance (wt_1: 3 retry events, incl. one double-retry chain in WF_104_8).
- All other activity × resource combos: failure probability = 0 (no failures observed).

### 3.2 inter-arrival-times-agent

- **Population**: all **38 released cases, including the 3 excluded failure-only cases** — arrivals are real system inputs regardless of outcome.
- Release time per case = timestamp of the `scheduled` row of the first activity (`/hbw/unload`).
- **Two-regime process** (per release-control analysis — do **not** model the mixed mean IAT of 140.3 s, cv 2.0):
  - **Gaps** between bursts: 13 gaps (mean 394.7 s, median 294.1 s) — extract the gap process,
  - **Burst sizes**: 14 bursts (size 1–9, mean 2.7) — extract the discrete size distribution,
  - **Within-burst IAT**: burst IATs (mean 2.44 s, median 1.44 s) — extract the short-interval process.
- Output: the three component samples (gaps, burst sizes, within-burst IAT) for the distribution-fitting agent.

### 3.3 quantities-quality-agent — skipped

No quantity or quality columns exist in the log (verified against the column mapping: no batch/quantity fields, no defect or inspection-result columns; `parameters` carries only routing detail such as positions, hbw slot, burn size/thickness). Scrap at the quality gate is already quantified by the topology (24 early exits, mostly at/after `/hw/human_review`, with per-variant `early_exit_after` probabilities in the spec) — no further extraction is needed.

### 3.4 distribution-fitting-agent

Fit and validate distributions for every extracted parameter:
1. **Service times** — per activity (or per split activity × resource where the durations agent confirmed a real difference); candidate families to review (e.g. lognormal, gamma, Weibull, constant); report recommended distribution + parameters + goodness-of-fit.
2. **Arrival gaps** — candidate families for the long inter-burst gaps (e.g. exponential, lognormal, gamma).
3. **Burst sizes** — discrete distribution (e.g. geometric/Poisson/empirical).
4. **Within-burst IAT** — short-interval process (e.g. exponential).
5. **Retry delays** — small sample (3 events); report empirical values; fit only if a distribution is defensible, otherwise recommend fixed/empirical values.
6. **Planned vs. actual comparison** — per-activity ratio and deviation statistics for validation (planned set from 3.1-B).

## 4. Exclusions & Skips (summary)

| Item | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|
| WF_102_16, WF_102_17, WF_104_9 | Excluded from failure-probability estimation; **included** in arrivals | Terminal failures with no recovery = truncation artifacts; releases are still real inputs. |
| 9 failed instances | Kept; durations recorded separately from the 452 successful ones | Real factory behavior; feed failure/retry model, not nominal service distribution. |
| `complete_service_time` | Not used as service duration | Includes queueing (mean 73.6 s vs 30.4 s actual service). |
| Quantities/quality extraction | Skipped | No such columns in the log; early-exit statistics already in spec. |
| Censored durations | None to handle | end_missing = 0; early exits occur after completed activities. |

## 5. Data Notes for Sub-Agents

1. Duration convention is start-row-based (end − start on `start` rows); do not use `complete`-row timestamps or `complete_service_time` for service times.
2. One missing value in `parameters` (on a `complete` row) — irrelevant to extraction.
3. Two instances have 2 distinct end values across their rows — negligible, no action.
4. `/hbw/store_empty_bucket` failures (hbw_2) have **no** retry instance — model as failure-without-retry (process absorbs the fault), distinct from wt_1 retry-on-same-resource.
5. hbw queue is priority-based (store > get_empty_bucket > store_empty_bucket > unload) and vgr is FIFO — relevant context for interpreting waiting times, but queue discipline is already in the spec and needs no extraction.

# Inter-Arrival Times Report — fischertechnik_lab_B (significant-hilarious-cuscus)

## 1. Population & Release-Time Convention

- **Population**: all **38 released cases**, including the 3 excluded failure-only cases (WF_102_16, WF_102_17, WF_104_9) — their releases are real system inputs regardless of outcome.
- **Release time per case** = timestamp of the `scheduled` row of the first activity `/hbw/unload`.
- Verified: for all 38 cases the earliest log timestamp of the case equals the `/hbw/unload` scheduled timestamp exactly (max abs diff 0.0 s), and `/hbw/unload` is the first activity of every case — so the release-time convention and the earliest-timestamp-per-case convention coincide.
- Window: first release 2021-06-30 15:24:34.013 (t0), last release 16:51:03.396; span of releases ≈ 5189.4 s.

## 2. Overall IAT Statistics (no gaps removed)

37 inter-arrival times over 38 cases:

| Statistic | Value (s) |
|---|---|
| Mean | 140.25 |
| Std | 280.42 |
| CV | 2.00 |
| Median | 3.19 |
| Min | 0.56 |
| Max | 1336.65 |

The mixed mean IAT (140.3 s, cv 2.0) is **not** a usable arrival model: it blends two very different regimes (short within-burst intervals and long idle gaps). The regimes are well separated (log-separation 0.88, gap-to-burst ratio ≈ 162, threshold 17.85 s), so the arrival process is modeled as **two_regime_bursts**.

## 3. Regime Decomposition (two_regime_bursts)

Threshold 17.85 s splits the 37 IATs into 13 inter-burst gaps and 24 within-burst IATs, forming **14 bursts** (first burst at t0; the 13 gaps separate the 14 bursts).

### 3.1 Gaps between bursts (n = 13)

|---|---|
| Mean | 394.67 |

| Median | 294.14 |
| Min | 32.27 |
| Max | 1336.65 |

Sample: [858.66, 1336.65, 478.22, 61.95, 193.35, 239.22, 189.61, 524.73, 32.27, 294.14, 199.43, 423.18, 299.32]

### 3.2 Burst sizes (n = 14 bursts)

# Extraction Plan Report — fischertechnik_lab_B (significant-hilarious-cuscus)

## 1. Scope & Data Basis

- **Data**: cleaned event log — 1,383 rows, 461 activity instances, 38 cases (workpieces), 20 activities, 15 resources (all capacity 1), 9 process-model variants, window ≈ 5,944 s (~99 min).
- **Duration convention**: actual service duration = end − start taken on the `start` row only (mean 30.4 s, min 0.0 s, max 218.7 s). `complete_service_time` (scheduled→complete, incl. queueing; mean 73.6 s) is a reference metric only — **never** used as service duration.
- **Censoring**: none for durations (end_missing = 0; every instance has a complete row). The 24 early-exit cases stop *after* a completed activity, so no censored service times.
- **Excluded cases** (truncation artifacts — terminal failure, no recovery): WF_102_16, WF_102_17, WF_104_9. Excluded from failure-probability and routing estimation; **included in arrival estimation** (their releases are real system inputs).

## 2. Agent Deployment Recommendation

| Sub-Agent | Deploy? | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| durations-processing-times-agent | **Yes** | 461 instances with full start/end pairs; service times per activity-resource, planned durations, and failure/retry parameters all extractable. |
| inter-arrival-times-agent | **Yes** | 38 releases under open (bursty) release control; two-regime gap/burst process must be extracted and fit. |
| quantities-quality-agent | **No** | No quantity or quality columns exist in the log (no batch sizes, defect counts, or inspection-result columns). Scrap/quality-gate behavior is already captured by the topology's early-exit statistics. |
| distribution-fitting-agent | **Yes** | Distribution review is always required: service times, arrival gaps, burst sizes, within-burst IAT, and retry delays all need fitted distributions with goodness-of-fit checks. |

## 3. Extraction Plan per Agent

### 3.1 durations-processing-times-agent

**A. Actual service times**
- Source: `start` rows only; duration = end − start.
- **Grouping strategy**: start at **activity × resource** level. For high-volume activities, test whether duration genuinely differs across resources and **split only where the difference is real and measurable**; otherwise pool to activity level. High-volume activities to check:
  - `/vgr/pick_up_and_transport` (127 instances; vgr_1 = in-process transport vs vgr_2 = initial pick-up — different roles, likely different durations),
  - `/ov/burn` (ov_1 vs ov_2 — different ovens; burn size/thickness parameters differ),
  - `/mm/mill` (mm_1 vs mm_2),
  - `/wt/pick_up_and_transport` (wt_1 vs wt_2),
  - `/hbw/store_empty_bucket` (hbw_2 only — no split possible).
- **Low-sample combos (n < 10)**: pool within resource class (e.g. mm_1+mm_2, ov_1+ov_2, wt_1+wt_2, sm_1+sm_2, vgr_1+vgr_2, hbw_1+hbw_2) rather than estimating per-resource.
- **Successful vs. failed instances**: build the service-time distribution from the 452 successful instances; record the 9 failed attempts' durations separately (failed attempts may run differently and feed the failure/retry model, not the nominal service distribution).
- **Data notes**: min duration is 0.0 s — flag zero/near-zero instances (possible instantaneous hand-off steps) before fitting; `/hw/human_review` (30 instances) is human-driven and expected to be high-variance.

**B. Planned durations (separate set)**
- Parse `planned_operation_time` (22 distinct values, 5–222 s) per activity as a **separate planned-duration set** for comparison/validation against actuals (ratio actual/planned per activity; flag activities where actuals systematically deviate from plan).

**C. Failure & retry parameters (explicit — do not defer to manual modeling)**
- **Failure probability per activity × resource**: failed instances / total instances, estimated from the 6 retryable failures only (the 3 excluded terminal failures are truncation artifacts and are **not** used for failure-rate estimation):
  - `/wt/pick_up_and_transport` on wt_1: 4 failed attempts (WF_104_8 ×2 consecutive, WF_109_6, WF_1107_7),
  - `/hbw/store_empty_bucket` on hbw_2: 2 failed attempts (WF_102_15, WF_104_8) — **no retry instance** (transient fault absorbed; case continued) → model as failure-without-retry.
- **Retry delay**: for each retryable failure, delay = start of the retry instance − complete of the failed instance (wt_1: 3 retry events, incl. one double-retry chain in WF_104_8).
- All other activity × resource combos: failure probability = 0 (no failures observed).

### 3.2 inter-arrival-times-agent

- **Population**: all **38 released cases, including the 3 excluded failure-only cases** — arrivals are real system inputs regardless of outcome.
- Release time per case = timestamp of the `scheduled` row of the first activity (`/hbw/unload`).
- **Two-regime process** (per release-control analysis — do **not** model the mixed mean IAT of 140.3 s, cv 2.0):
  - **Gaps** between bursts: 13 gaps (mean 394.7 s, median 294.1 s) — extract the gap process,
  - **Burst sizes**: 14 bursts (size 1–9, mean 2.7) — extract the discrete size distribution,
  - **Within-burst IAT**: burst IATs (mean 2.44 s, median 1.44 s) — extract the short-interval process.
- Output: the three component samples (gaps, burst sizes, within-burst IAT) for the distribution-fitting agent.

### 3.3 quantities-quality-agent — skipped

No quantity or quality columns exist in the log (verified against the column mapping: no batch/quantity fields, no defect or inspection-result columns; `parameters` carries only routing detail such as positions, hbw slot, burn size/thickness). Scrap at the quality gate is already quantified by the topology (24 early exits, mostly at/after `/hw/human_review`, with per-variant `early_exit_after` probabilities in the spec) — no further extraction is needed.

### 3.4 distribution-fitting-agent

Fit and validate distributions for every extracted parameter:
1. **Service times** — per activity (or per split activity × resource where the durations agent confirmed a real difference); candidate families to review (e.g. lognormal, gamma, Weibull, constant); report recommended distribution + parameters + goodness-of-fit.
2. **Arrival gaps** — candidate families for the long inter-burst gaps (e.g. exponential, lognormal, gamma).
3. **Burst sizes** — discrete distribution (e.g. geometric/Poisson/empirical).
4. **Within-burst IAT** — short-interval process (e.g. exponential).
5. **Retry delays** — small sample (3 events); report empirical values; fit only if a distribution is defensible, otherwise recommend fixed/empirical values.
6. **Planned vs. actual comparison** — per-activity ratio and deviation statistics for validation (planned set from 3.1-B).

## 4. Exclusions & Skips (summary)

| Item | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|

## 2. Agent Deployment Recommendation

| Sub-Agent | Deploy? | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| durations-processing-times-agent | **Yes** | 461 instances with full start/end pairs; service times per activity-resource, planned durations, and failure/retry parameters all extractable. |
| inter-arrival-times-agent | **Yes** | 38 releases under open (bursty) release control; two-regime gap/burst process must be extracted and fit. |
| quantities-quality-agent | **No** | No quantity or quality columns exist in the log (no batch sizes, defect counts, or inspection-result columns). Scrap/quality-gate behavior is already captured by the topology's early-exit statistics. |
| distribution-fitting-agent | **Yes** | Distribution review is always required: service times, arrival gaps, burst sizes, within-burst IAT, and retry delays all need fitted distributions with goodness-of-fit checks. |

## 3. Extraction Plan per Agent

### 3.1 durations-processing-times-agent

**A. Actual service times**
- Source: `start` rows only; duration = end − start.
- **Grouping strategy**: start at **activity × resource** level. For high-volume activities, test whether duration genuinely differs across resources and **split only where the difference is real and measurable**; otherwise pool to activity level. High-volume activities to check:
  - `/vgr/pick_up_and_transport` (127 instances; vgr_1 = in-process transport vs vgr_2 = initial pick-up — different roles, likely different durations),
  - `/ov/burn` (ov_1 vs ov_2 — different ovens; burn size/thickness parameters differ),
  - `/mm/mill` (mm_1 vs mm_2),
  - `/wt/pick_up_and_transport` (wt_1 vs wt_2),
  - `/hbw/store_empty_bucket` (hbw_2 only — no split possible).
- **Low-sample combos (n < 10)**: pool within resource class (e.g. mm_1+mm_2, ov_1+ov_2, wt_1+wt_2, sm_1+sm_2, vgr_1+vgr_2, hbw_1+hbw_2) rather than estimating per-resource.
- **Successful vs. failed instances**: build the service-time distribution from the 452 successful instances; record the 9 failed attempts' durations separately (failed attempts may run differently and feed the failure/retry model, not the nominal service distribution).
- **Data notes**: min duration is 0.0 s — flag zero/near-zero instances (possible instantaneous hand-off steps) before fitting; `/hw/human_review` (30 instances) is human-driven and expected to be high-variance.

**B. Planned durations (separate set)**
- Parse `planned_operation_time` (22 distinct values, 5–222 s) per activity as a **separate planned-duration set** for comparison/validation against actuals (ratio actual/planned per activity; flag activities where actuals systematically deviate from plan).

**C. Failure & retry parameters (explicit — do not defer to manual modeling)**
- **Failure probability per activity × resource**: failed instances / total instances, estimated from the 6 retryable failures only (the 3 excluded terminal failures are truncation artifacts and are **not** used for failure-rate estimation):
  - `/wt/pick_up_and_transport` on wt_1: 4 failed attempts (WF_104_8 ×2 consecutive, WF_109_6, WF_1107_7),
  - `/hbw/store_empty_bucket` on hbw_2: 2 failed attempts (WF_102_15, WF_104_8) — **no retry instance** (transient fault absorbed; case continued) → model as failure-without-retry.
- **Retry delay**: for each retryable failure, delay = start of the retry instance − complete of the failed instance (wt_1: 3 retry events, incl. one double-retry chain in WF_104_8).
- All other activity × resource combos: failure probability = 0 (no failures observed).

- **Population**: all **38 released cases, including the 3 excluded failure-only cases** — arrivals are real system inputs regardless of outcome.
- Release time per case = timestamp of the `scheduled` row of the first activity (`/hbw/unload`).
- **Two-regime process** (per release-control analysis — do **not** model the mixed mean IAT of 140.3 s, cv 2.0):
  - **Gaps** between bursts: 13 gaps (mean 394.7 s, median 294.1 s) — extract the gap process,
  - **Burst sizes**: 14 bursts (size 1–9, mean 2.7) — extract the discrete size distribution,
  - **Within-burst IAT**: burst IATs (mean 2.44 s, median 1.44 s) — extract the short-interval process.
- Output: the three component samples (gaps, burst sizes, within-burst IAT) for the distribution-fitting agent.

### 3.3 quantities-quality-agent — skipped

No quantity or quality columns exist in the log (verified against the column mapping: no batch/quantity fields, no defect or inspection-result columns; `parameters` carries only routing detail such as positions, hbw slot, burn size/thickness). Scrap at the quality gate is already quantified by the topology (24 early exits, mostly at/after `/hw/human_review`, with per-variant `early_exit_after` probabilities in the spec) — no further extraction is needed.

### 3.4 distribution-fitting-agent

Fit and validate distributions for every extracted parameter:
1. **Service times** — per activity (or per split activity × resource where the durations agent confirmed a real difference); candidate families to review (e.g. lognormal, gamma, Weibull, constant); report recommended distribution + parameters + goodness-of-fit.

# Column Mapping Report — fischertechnik_lab_B (significant-hilarious-cuscus)

## 1. Dataset Summary

- **Source**: `work_files/eventlog.parquet` → cleaned: `work_files/eventlog_cleaned.parquet`
- **Shape**: 1,383 rows × 20 columns (raw); 1,383 rows × 12 columns (cleaned)
- **Structure**: lifecycle layout — exactly 3 rows per activity instance (`scheduled` → `start` → `complete`), 461 instances, 38 cases (workpieces), 20 activities, 15 resources, 9 process-model variants.
- **Time span**: t0 = 2021-06-30T15:24:34Z, horizon T ≈ 5,943.7 s (~99 min).
- **Outcomes**: 452 success, 9 failure (kept — real factory behavior; HTTP 418/401 on the `complete` row).
- **No duplicate rows**; no missing values in key columns.

## 2. Column Mapping

| Column | Meaning | Simulation Role | Sim-Relevant | Action |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `time:timestamp` | Timestamp of the lifecycle transition (ISO8601, mixed precision) | Request time on `scheduled` row; **service start** on `start` row | Yes | Keep; parse to seconds. Actual duration = `operation_end_time` − `time:timestamp` on `start` rows only |
| `operation_end_time` | Operation end timestamp (ISO8601) | **Service end** (preferred over `time:timestamp` of the `complete` row) | Yes | Keep; parse to seconds |
| `lifecycle:transition` | Transition type: `scheduled` / `start` / `complete` | Lifecycle column | Yes | Keep |
| `lifecycle:state` | `assigned` (scheduled) / `inProgress` (start) / `success` / `failure` (complete) | Outcome column; 9 failures retained | Yes | Keep |
| `event_id` | Integer id shared by the 3 rows of an instance (1002–1483) | Redundant instance key | No | **Drop** (keep `identifier:id`) |
| `identifier:id` | Activity-instance id (e.g. `a_15513`), unique per instance | Instance column linking the 3 lifecycle rows | Yes | Keep |
| `process_model_id` | Process-model / product variant (WF_101…WF_1107), 9 values | Variant column | Yes | Keep |
| `case` | Workpiece id, e.g. `WF_101_13` (prefix = process model, 100% consistent) | Case column | Yes | Keep |
| `concept:name` | Activity name (e.g. `/ov/burn`, `/vgr/pick_up_and_transport`), 20 values | Activity column | Yes | Keep |
| `requested_service_url` | REST URL of the service call; resource query param matches `org:resource` 100% | Redundant (resource already mapped); carries size/thickness for burn | No | **Drop** (parameters carry the same info) |
| `org:resource` | Executing resource (vgr_1/2, hbw_1/2, mm_1/2, ov_1, hw_1, wt_1/2, sm_1, …), 15 values | Resource column | Yes | Keep |
| `planned_operation_time` | Planned duration, timedelta string (e.g. `0 days 00:00:47`) | Planned processing time | Yes | Keep; **parse to seconds** (22 distinct values, 5–222 s) |
| `parameters` | Dict string of activity parameters (positions, hbw slot, burn size/thickness, NFC flag); 1 missing on a `complete` row | Activity parameters (routing/variant detail) | Yes | Keep |
| `case:concept:name` | Identical to `case` (100%) | Redundant | No | **Drop** |
| `SubProcessID` | UUID present only on `start` rows (459/461) | Redundant instance detail | No | **Drop** |
| `current_task` | Free-text task description, only on `start` rows | Redundant narrative | No | **Drop** |
| `response_status_code` | HTTP code on `complete` rows (200 / 418×7 / 401×2) | Redundant with `lifecycle:state` (success↔200, failure↔418/401, 100% consistent) | No | **Drop** |
| `complete_service_time` | Full response time scheduled→complete incl. queueing (timedelta string), only on `complete` rows | Reference metric (mean 73.6 s vs 30.4 s actual service) | Yes | Keep (do not use as service duration) |
| `human_workstation_green_button_pressed` | 1/0 flag, only on `/hw/human_review` instances (87 rows) | Human-intervention detail; not needed for core simulation | No | **Drop** |
| `unsatisfied_condition_description` | Precondition-failure detail (NFC/light-barrier/warehouse errors), only on the 9 failed instances | Diagnostic detail of failures | No | **Drop** |

## 3. Log Schema (confirmed via `set_log_schema`)

- **Layout**: lifecycle — one row per transition; 3 rows per instance.
- **case_col**: `case` | **activity_col**: `concept:name` | **resource_col**: `org:resource` | **variant_col**: `process_model_id`
- **start_col**: `time:timestamp` | **end_col**: `operation_end_time` (preferred over `complete`-row timestamp)
- **lifecycle_col**: `lifecycle:transition` | **instance_col**: `identifier:id`
- **enabled_value**: `scheduled` (queue entry / request) | **start_value**: `start` | **complete_value**: `complete`
- **state_col**: `lifecycle:state` | success: `success` | failure: `failure`
- **Validation**: 461 instances, 38 cases, 20 activities, 15 resources; `enabled_observed_frac = 1.0` (waiting times fully observable); `end_missing = 0`; no warnings. Sample verified: e.g. `/hbw/unload` on `hbw_2`: enabled 0.0 s → start 3.56 s → end 55.91 s (≈ start + 52 s planned).
- **Duration convention**: actual service duration = `operation_end_time − time:timestamp` on `start` rows only (mean 30.4 s, min 0.0, max 218.7 s, no negatives). `complete_service_time` records the full response time (scheduled → complete, incl. queueing; mean 73.6 s, max 1,079 s) and is kept only as a reference metric.

## 4. Excluded Columns

`event_id`, `case:concept:name`, `SubProcessID`, `current_task`, `response_status_code`, `requested_service_url`, `unsatisfied_condition_description`, `human_workstation_green_button_pressed` (8 columns; all redundant or diagnostic-only).

## 5. Cleaning Summary

- Dropped 8 columns (above).
- Drop rows with missing values in key columns (`identifier:id`, `case`, `concept:name`, `org:resource`, `time:timestamp`, `operation_end_time`, `lifecycle:transition`, `lifecycle:state`): **0 rows removed** (no missing values in these columns).
- Duplicate rows: none.
- Result: 1,383 rows × 12 columns → `eventlog_cleaned.parquet`.
- All 9 `failure` entries in `lifecycle:state` retained (real factory behavior).

## 6. Remaining Ambiguities

- `operation_end_time` differs across the 3 rows of an instance (per-row operation end, not a constant); the schema uses the value on the relevant row, which is consistent with the duration convention above.
- `parameters` has 1 missing value (on a `complete` row); kept as-is since it is not a key column.
- 2 instances have only 2 distinct `operation_end_time` values across their rows (negligible; no action taken).

df = pd.read_parquet("eventlog_cleaned.parquet")

st['oe'] = pd.to_datetime(st['operation_end_time'], format='ISO8601')
st['duration'] = (st['oe'] - st['ts']).dt.total_seconds()
comp = df[df['lifecycle:transition']=='complete'][['identifier:id','lifecycle:state']].rename(columns={'lifecycle:state':'outcome'})
st = st.merge(comp, on='identifier:id', how='left')
st['planned'] = pd.to_timedelta(st['planned_operation_time']).dt.total_seconds()

g['cv'] = g['std']/g['mean']
print(g.to_string())
print()

import pandas as pd, numpy as np
from scipy import stats
pd.set_option('display.width', 250)
st = pd.read_parquet("instances.parquet")

# Split tests for high-volume activities (all instances, successes + failures)
for act, res in [('/vgr/pick_up_and_transport', ['vgr_1','vgr_2']),
                 ('/ov/burn', ['ov_1','ov_2']),
                 ('/mm/mill', ['mm_1','mm_2']),
                 ('/wt/pick_up_and_transport', ['wt_1','wt_2'])]:
    a = st[(st['concept:name']==act) & (st['org:resource']==res[0])]['duration']
    b = st[(st['concept:name']==act) & (st['org:resource']==res[1])]['duration']
    t, pval = stats.ttest_ind(a, b, equal_var=False)
    # overlap of ranges
    print(f"{act}: {res[0]} n={len(a)} mean={a.mean():.2f} std={a.std():.2f} range=[{a.min():.1f},{a.max():.1f}] | "
          f"{res[1]} n={len(b)} mean={b.mean():.2f} std={b.std():.2f} range=[{b.min():.1f},{b.max():.1f}] | "
          f"Welch t={t:.2f} p={pval:.2e}")

# also check /hbw/store_empty_bucket (hbw_1 n=1 vs hbw_2 n=36) and /sm/sort (10 vs 6)
for act, res in [('/hbw/store_empty_bucket', ['hbw_1','hbw_2']),
                 ('/sm/sort', ['sm_1','sm_2']),
                 ('/sm/transport', ['sm_1','sm_2']),
                 ('/mm/deburr', ['mm_1','mm_2'])]:
    a = st[(st['concept:name']==act) & (st['org:resource']==res[0])]['duration']
    b = st[(st['concept:name']==act) & (st['org:resource']==res[1])]['duration']
    t, pval = stats.ttest_ind(a, b, equal_var=False) if len(a)>1 and len(b)>1 else (np.nan, np.nan)
    print(f"{act}: {res[0]} n={len(a)} mean={a.mean():.2f} std={a.std() if len(a)>1 else 0:.2f} | {res[1]} n={len(b)} mean={b.mean():.2f} std={b.std():.2f} | t={t:.2f} p={pval:.2e}")
